subject: Nanotechnology
title: Magnetic Nanoparticle Imaging
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Magnetic Nanoparticle Imaging.

hook.text: Iron oxide nanoparticles make MRI scans sharper — darkening tissue where they accumulate.

buildup.text: Superparamagnetic particles disturb the local magnetic field, shortening water proton relaxation times.

discovery.text: Targeted iron particles highlight tumors, inflammation, or blood clots that would otherwise be invisible on MRI.

twist.text: Magnetic particle imaging, or MPI, is a new modality — it directly detects the particles, not water around them.

climax.text: MPI offers real-time 3D imaging with zero radiation — clinical trials are underway for vascular imaging.

punchline.text: Tiny magnets light up disease that MRI alone would miss.

quiz.question: How do iron oxide nanoparticles enhance MRI?
options: They emit radio waves detected by the scanner
They alter local magnetic fields, changing water proton relaxation for contrast
They reflect ultrasound waves for imaging
